This guide gets phwstyle installed and ready on your computer. It covers the
install routes, what to do when an install fails, a check of what is ready,
the Ubuntu font, the Public Health Wales logo and the package options. Once
it is done, [Getting started](phwstyle.html) shows what to make first.

phwstyle needs R 4.3 or later and ggplot2 3.5 or later. The Quarto formats
need Quarto 1.5 or later.

## Install phwstyle

phwstyle is not on CRAN yet, so install it from GitHub:

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Ch3w3y/phwstyle-r", dependencies = TRUE)
```

`dependencies = TRUE` also installs the optional packages for every output
type (flextable, reactable, plotly, bslib, ragg and others). Leave it out for a
smaller install. Functions that need an optional package offer to install it
the first time you use them.

### Faster installs with Posit Package Manager

Posit Package Manager (P3M) has ready-built copies of the packages phwstyle
uses, so nothing needs compiling. Point R at it before installing. On Linux,
use the address for your distribution from the
[P3M setup page](https://packagemanager.posit.co/client/#/repos/cran/setup).

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest"))
remotes::install_github("Ch3w3y/phwstyle-r", dependencies = TRUE)
```

### With uvr

In a [uvr](https://nbafrank.github.io/uvr/) project, add the package from
GitHub:

```sh
uvr add Ch3w3y/phwstyle-r@main
```

### From the release file

If GitHub can't be reached from your computer, install the built package from
the [releases page](https://github.com/Ch3w3y/phwstyle-r/releases). Change
the version in the address to the latest release.

```r
install.packages(c("cli", "ggplot2", "gtable", "htmltools", "rlang",
                   "scales", "systemfonts", "tidyselect", "zip"))
install.packages(
  "https://github.com/Ch3w3y/phwstyle-r/releases/download/v0.2.0/phwstyle_0.2.0.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

Once phwstyle is on CRAN, `install.packages("phwstyle", dependencies = TRUE)`
will work too.

## If the install fails on a managed computer

The last line of the error names a file in your Temp folder, such as
`installation of package 'C:/Users/.../Temp/.../phwstyle_0.2.0.tar.gz' had
non-zero exit status`. That is only where R unpacked the download. The cause is
a few lines further up. Find it in this list.

**`LoadLibrary failure: This program is blocked by group policy`** (Windows).
Your organisation only lets code run from approved folders, and the folder R
installs packages into is not one of them. Nothing is wrong with phwstyle,
because any package with compiled code fails the same way. Try `library(rlang)`
to see. Moving the temporary folder or installing from the release file does
not help. Ask IT which folder is approved for R packages, or to approve your R
library, which `.libPaths()[1]` shows. If they give you a folder, add it to
your `.Renviron` file and restart R. `usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens the file.

```
R_LIBS_USER=C:/the/approved/folder
```

**"Do you want to install from sources the package which needs
compilation?"** Answer no. R then uses the ready-built version, which is what
you want unless Rtools is installed.

**`'configure' exists but is not executable`** (Linux servers). The packages
phwstyle depends on compile from source by default, and the temporary folder
does not allow programs to run. Install the dependencies from Posit Package
Manager, as above, which avoids compiling. Or give R a temporary folder you
control by adding `TMPDIR=/home/your.name/tmp` to `.Renviron`. Create the
folder first.

**GitHub cannot be reached.** Use the release file above.

A policy that only blocks programs in the Temp folder doesn't stop phwstyle
installing, and neither does an accented letter in your user name.

## Check your setup

Run the check once after installing. It lists what is ready and what is
missing, with the command that fixes each item.

```{r}
library(phwstyle)
phw_setup_check(install = FALSE)
```

It checks the Ubuntu font on your computer, the logo, the optional R packages
for each type of output, Pandoc, Quarto and XeLaTeX. Your results will differ
from the ones above. In an interactive session, `phw_setup_check()` with no
arguments also offers to install the missing R packages and the font. The
function returns the checks as a data frame, invisibly.

If you skip the check, phwstyle reminds you when it loads and something is
missing. Set `options(phwstyle.quiet = TRUE)` to hide the reminder.

## Fonts

phwstyle uses the Ubuntu typeface, which ships with the package. `phw_font()`
returns the family name that phwstyle will use. It falls back to Arial and then
to `"sans"` when Ubuntu can't be used.

```{r}
phw_font()
```

Most outputs need nothing from you. phwstyle registers the bundled font with
systemfonts when the package loads, so ragg, svglite and the Word and
PowerPoint outputs in officer and flextable can find it. That is
`phw_register_fonts()`, which you can also call yourself. It returns `TRUE`
invisibly when the fonts are registered.

```{r}
phw_register_fonts()
```

HTML outputs and the phwstyle PDF formats carry the font with them.

Run `phw_install_fonts()` once per computer when you open phwstyle's output in
Word or PowerPoint on your own computer, draw with base R devices such as
`pdf()`, or build LaTeX documents outside the phwstyle formats. It copies the
font files into your personal font folder and asks first.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
phw_install_fonts()
```

If you build HTML by hand, attach `phw_font_dependency()` so the font works on
computers that don't have it. The font files are bundled, so nothing is
fetched from the internet.

```{r}
phw_font_dependency()$name
```

For example, `htmltools::tagList(phw_font_dependency(), your_html)` attaches it
to a piece of HTML.

To use another family everywhere, set `options(phwstyle.font = "Arial")`.

## Logos

The Public Health Wales logo is a trade mark and is not included in the
package. Without a logo, every output is still styled and shows the
organisation name instead. `phw_has_logo()` tells you whether phwstyle can
find one.

```{r}
phw_has_logo()
```

There are two ways to provide the logo:

* Run `phw_download_logos()` once per computer. It downloads the bilingual logo
  from phw.nhs.wales, makes blue, white and black versions in SVG and PNG, and
  stores them in your user cache folder. It asks before it downloads.
* Set `options(phwstyle.logo_dir = "path/to/folder")` to a folder with your own
  copies of the files.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
phw_download_logos()
```

`phw_logo()` returns the path of one version, or `NULL` when no logo is
available. Choose the `"blue"` version for white backgrounds, `"white"` for the
gradient band or any dark background, and `"black"` for mono print. Pass
`format = "svg"` for the vector file.

```{r}
phw_logo("white", format = "svg")
```

`phw_graphic()` returns the path of a graphic phwstyle draws itself, which
contains no logo. The `"band"` is the header gradient, `"cover"` is the A4
portrait cover background and `"cover_wide"` is the 16:9 slide background.

```{r}
basename(phw_graphic("band"))
```

The examples in these guides run without the logo. See `inst/COPYRIGHTS` in
the package for the licences of the bundled files.

## Package options

Set an option once, for example in your `.Rprofile` or at the top of a
script. Each one has a default that works without you doing anything.

| Option | What it does | More in |
|---|---|---|
| `phwstyle.palette` | The default palette name, such as `"accessible"`, used by every chart, table and widget. | [Colours](colours.html#colour-blind-safe-colours) |
| `PHWSTYLE_PALETTE` (environment variable) | The same switch for one render, such as `PHWSTYLE_PALETTE=accessible quarto render report.qmd`. | [Reports, slides and dashboards](documents.html#default-and-accessible-colours) |
| `phwstyle.font` | The font family to use instead of Ubuntu. | [Fonts](#fonts) |
| `phwstyle.logo_dir` | The folder with your own logo files. | [Logos](#logos) |
| `phwstyle.key_file` | The CSV file that colour keys are read from and saved to, so colours stay the same across sessions. `phw_key_file()` sets it for you. | [Colours](colours.html#colours-that-stay-with-their-groups) |
| `phwstyle.boundary_dir` | The folder where downloaded boundaries are cached. | [Maps](maps.html#keeping-boundaries-up-to-date) |
| `phwstyle.boundary_update` | `FALSE` stops `phw_boundaries()` checking each week for a newer list of boundary releases. | [Maps](maps.html#keeping-boundaries-up-to-date) |
| `phwstyle.quiet` | `TRUE` hides the reminder that appears when the package loads. | [Check your setup](#check-your-setup) |

For example:

```r
options(
  phwstyle.palette = "accessible",
  phwstyle.key_file = "phw-colours.csv",
  phwstyle.quiet = TRUE
)
```
